page.title: What Does Community as a Service Cost?
page.description: Understand the scope factors that drive Community as a Service pricing, which tasks to keep in-house, common platforms, and what a managed engagement includes.
page.h1: What does Community as a Service cost?
page.definition: Community as a Service is a managed offering where an external team handles moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting on platforms such as Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups while the client retains strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions.
page.quick_answer: Request a scoped quote based on coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming needs; there is no fixed price list.

sections.h2: What factors determine Community as a Service pricing?

blocks.p: Pricing is quoted per engagement and scales with coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming complexity.

ul: Coverage hours across time zones and weekends
Moderation risk level and policy complexity
Programming cadence such as events, AMAs and content series

sections.h2: Which community tasks should stay in-house versus outsourced?

blocks.p: Strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions remain internal while operational execution moves to the service provider.

sections.h2: What platforms are commonly used for Community as a Service?

blocks.p: Engagements run on the platform the organization already uses or selects during the scoping phase.

ul: Discord for real-time chat and voice
Slack for professional and workplace communities
Circle for branded member spaces with courses
Higher Logic for association and member-based groups
LinkedIn groups for professional network adjacency

sections.h2: How do coverage hours and member volume affect cost?

blocks.p: Higher coverage demands and larger member bases increase staffing needs and tooling costs, which are reflected in the scoped quote.

A community requiring twenty-four-seven moderation across multiple time zones needs a larger rotation of moderators than one covered during business hours only. Member volume drives queue size for support tickets, onboarding throughput and the frequency of proactive outreach. Moderation risk escalates with public-facing communities, regulated industries or sensitive topics, requiring senior reviewers and faster escalation paths. Programming complexity adds producer hours for event planning, speaker coordination and content calendar management.

sections.h2: What does a typical Community as a Service engagement include?

blocks.p: A scoped engagement delivers ongoing operations across moderation, support, programming, onboarding and reporting with a named team.

ol: Dedicated community manager as primary point of contact
Moderation team covering agreed hours and escalation paths
Member support handling tickets, questions and disputes
Programming calendar with recurring events and content drops
Onboarding flow design and new-member welcome sequence
Monthly health report with growth, engagement and sentiment metrics
Quarterly strategy review with stakeholder alignment session

sections.h2: How long does it take to launch a managed community?

blocks.p: Launch timeline depends on platform readiness, policy development and team onboarding, typically spanning several weeks.

If the platform is already live and policies exist, the service team can ramp moderation and support within two to three weeks. A net-new community requires platform configuration, guideline drafting, moderator training and a soft-launch period with founding members before full public opening. Complex migrations from one platform to another add data mapping, member communication and redirect setup. The first ninety days serve as a calibration window to adjust staffing, refine workflows and establish baseline metrics before the first quarterly review.

faq.q: Can I get a fixed monthly price for Community as a Service?
faq.a: West Peek Productions quotes Community as a Service by scope covering coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming; it does not publish a fixed price list.

faq.q: Do I need to move my community to a specific platform?
faq.a: Engagements run on the platform you already use such as Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic or LinkedIn groups; the service team adapts to your environment.

faq.q: What happens during a crisis or major incident?
faq.a: Crisis escalation authority stays in-house while the service team executes the agreed response plan, provides real-time moderation surge and delivers post-incident reporting within the scoped coverage.

faq.q: How is success measured in a managed community?
faq.a: Monthly health reports track growth, engagement, sentiment, response times and resolution rates; quarterly reviews align metrics with business goals and adjust scope as needed.

faq.q: Can the service team create community programming and events?
faq.a: Programming is a core outsourced workstream including recurring events, AMAs, content series and member-led initiatives; the calendar is co-owned and approved in the quarterly review.
